subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should `channels.telegram.accounts.<account>.direct.<peer>.tools` and `toolsBySender` remain a supported hard-enforcement surface for Telegram DMs, and should it be enforced through a shared direct-aware tool-policy resolver?
rationale: The schema and types already advertise a security-sensitive per-DM tool-policy surface, but current runtime enforcement does not read Telegram `direct` config; choosing enforcement, retirement, or deferral changes operator security expectations and config compatibility.

options.title: Enforce Direct DM Tool Policy
options.body: Treat the existing direct fields as supported and implement direct-aware policy resolution with exact, wildcard, account-scoped, threaded-DM, and sender-precedence regression coverage.

options.title: Retire The Accepted Surface
options.body: Remove, reject, or doctor-diagnose the direct tool-policy config so operators do not rely on a silent no-op security control.

options.title: Defer To Binding Policy Design
options.body: Keep this open but make the broader binding-policy decision the canonical product route, accepting that Telegram direct policy remains unreliable until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Enforce Direct DM Tool Policy
recommendation.body: Treat the existing direct fields as supported and implement direct-aware policy resolution with exact, wildcard, account-scoped, threaded-DM, and sender-precedence regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared tool-policy and trusted group-scope history makes this the closest current owner for the security-boundary decision.
